Doors to the City Council Chamber will open at 1:30 p.m. for Open Session. Please be mindful that
seating is limited and available on a first come, first served basis.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting
convenience:

  ¡  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.
  ¡  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video, at
  https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280, FAX at 310-412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard,
First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and

Inglewood, California
  June 27, 2023

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  June 27, 2023, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
  Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:02 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Finance
  Authority/ Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority Secretary announced the presence of
  a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/ Parking Authority
  Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/ Finance Authority Members/ Parking
  Authority Members/ Joint Powers Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/ Joint
  Powers Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance Authority,
  Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Finance Authority/ Parking Authority/ Joint
  Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Finance Authority/
  Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority on any item on the Agendas, other than the
  Public Hearings.

  Marvin McCoy, District 2 resident, commented on Agenda Item Nos. DR-1, Adoption of
  a resolution providing Champions Grant Assistance Awards to eligible Inglewood Small
  Businesses and Inglewood Nonprofit Organizations negatively impacted by the COVID-
  19 Public Health Emergency, 5, Approval of an eighth (8)-month Cooperative Purchase
  Agreement with New Tangram, LLC (Tangram), and 6, Authorization of a payment for an
  invoice submitted by Kelcey Newman dba: Attain Design and Marketing Communications.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated June
  22, 2023, in the amount of $3,960,902.62, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/ Successor Agency Members/ Housing Authority Members Gray,
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/ Successor Agency Chairman / Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes:  None.
 June 27, 2023

301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – CATEGORICAL EXEMPTION (EA-CE-2023-013)
  AFFIRMED; ORDINANCE NO. 23-14 INTRODUCED – APPROVAL OF ZONING
  CODE AMENDMENT 23-00001 (ZCA-23-00001) TO MODIFY CHAPTER 12 OF
  THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE. The City Clerk announced that the next
  scheduled matter was a public to consider introduction of an ordinance approving Zoning
  Code Amendment 23-00001 (ZCA-23-00001) to modify Chapter 12 of the Inglewood
  Municipal Code to permit automated car was facilities in the MU-C (Mixed-Use Corridor)
  Zone, notice was given in the time, form, and manner as required by law, an affidavit was
  on file, and no communications were received.
  Louis Atwell, Acting City Manager presented a Staff Report dated June 27, 2023.
  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager presented a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke concerning the over-proliferation of car washes and the
  extensive remodeling done on the car wash located on La Brea. He discussed his confusion
  about the staff’s presentation and the actions taken by a previous mayor to limit hair and beauty
  salons. He also discussed the number of members available at the Planning  Commission
  meeting. Finally, he addressed his concerns regarding well- connected people with money getting
  special treatment and adjacent car washes in the  City of Hawthorne.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comment portion at the hour of 2:11 p.m.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby affirm Categorical Exemption (EA-CE-2023-013).
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 23-14 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, TO APPROVE ZONING CODE AMENDMENT ZCA-23-00001
  TO PERMIT AUTOMATED CAR WASH FACILITIES IN THE MU-C
  (MIXED-USE CORRIDOR) ZONE CITYWIDE

  was introduced by Council Member Morales.

301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – CATEGORICAL EXEMPTION (EA-CE-2023-051)
  AFFIRMED; ORDINANCE NO. 23-15 INTRODUCED – AMENDING ARTICLE
  17.3 (SIGN OVERLAY ZONE) TO INCLUDE THE AMENDED MASTER SIGN
  PLAN FOR A 29.5-ACRE C-R (COMMERCIAL AND RECREATION) ZONED
  PROPERTY AT 3900 WEST MANCHESTER BOULEVARD. The City Clerk
  announced that the next scheduled matter was a public hearing to consider introduction of
  an ordinance approving Zoning Code Amendment 23-00003 (ZCA-23-00003) to amend
  Article 17.3 (Sign Overlay Zone) to include the amended Master Sign Plan for a 29.5-acre
  C-R (Commercial and Recreation) Zoned Property at 3900 West Manchester Boulevard,
  notice was given in the time, form, and manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file,
  and no communications were received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented a Staff Report dated June 27, 2023.

  2
 June 27, 2023

  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager presented a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke about two comment letters submitted regarding Zoning
  Code Amendment 23-00003. He discussed the two letters received from the KIA Forum and a
  law firm that represents WOW Media. The speaker addressed his feelings towards  the two
  letters not included in the Staff Report. Additionally, he discussed who sent the letters  and
  disputes regarding different companies within the city. Finally, he requested to  view the two
  letters received before the item was voted upon.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comment portion at the hour of 2:22 p.m.

  Furthermore, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Faulk that the City Council does hereby affirm Categorical Exemption (EA-CE-
  2023-051). The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 23-15 entitled:

  MASTER SIGN PLAN FOR 29.5 ACRE C-R (COMMERCIAL RECREATION)
  ZONED PROPERTY AT 3900 WEST MANCHESTER BOULEVARD

  was introduced by Council Member Padilla.
